quote: They needn’t have bothered with Stage 2. There was hostility almost from the moment each group became aware of the other group’s existence
content: The archive says otherwise. Sherif's first attempt at the study, at Middle Grove in 1953, failed because the boys refused to turn on one another and instead suspected the staff, who then abandoned the experiment; the Robbers Cave study was the second try, and its records show staff manipulating events at each stage, including staging the theft of belongings and steering the boys toward retaliation (Perry 2018, The Lost Boys, book, no DOI). The published account omits the failed first run. The study has 22 subjects, no control group, participant-observers who were also the experimenters, and no replication; the essay calls it as perfect an experiment "as any ever devised by social science," which, on the evidence of the archive, is a comment on social science. Intergroup hostility is real and easily produced, as the minimal-group experiments show with far cleaner methods. Robbers Cave is a story, and the storytellers were on the payroll.

quote: The Robbers Cave Experiment illustrates the psychology of hunter-gatherer bands, echoed through time, as perfectly as any experiment ever devised by social science.
content: The ethnography of hunter-gatherer bands does not look like Robbers Cave. Across 32 foraging societies, most co-resident adults in a band are unrelated, individuals move between bands throughout life, and the between-band network is dense with marriage, exchange and visiting (Hill et al. 2011); the standard picture is of fluid membership and cooperative relations among bands, with warfare varying enormously by ecology. Two fixed groups of eleven boys, sealed off from each other and set in competition for prizes by adults, is a model of a summer camp. The essay's leap from that to the ancestral human condition is the evolutionary just-so story that the sequence elsewhere says not to tell, and the parenthetical wish for a supervillain is a policy proposal derived from it.
